lines: Middle Eastern crisis Gaza war Gaza genocide Five Palestinians killed, including a child, and others injured with varying degrees of wounds in Israeli airstrikes on various areas of Gaza Strip In a continuous violation of the ceasefire agreement Signed in October 2025. (Anadolu Agency)

Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war, Israeli settler violence An attack by Israeli settlers on Palestinian homes in the village of Ein ad-Duyuk at-Tahta west of Jericho city In the occupied West Bank resulted in the death of a Palestinian elderly woman and the injury of ten others. (Al Jazeera)

2026 Iran war 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain Bahrain's military intercepts a number of drones fired by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) at Sheikh Isa Air Base. (Le Monde)
The United States Air Force conducts a series of at least six strikes on Qeshm Island. The IRGC shoots down a General Atomics MQ-9 Reaper drone south of the island. (News.am) (Le Monde)

Russo-Ukrainian war Crimea attacks The Crimean Bridge is struck by Ukrainian drones for the second day in a row, killing two people and prompting Russian authorities to close vehicle traffic again. Open-source intelligence report that a section of the road bridge damaged yesterday has collapsed into the Kerch Strait. (Reuters) (Türkiye)

Following the arrest of party leaders, activists of the banned Awami League and Chhatra League mobilize via mosque loudspeakers and storm and set fire to a police station in Tungipara, Gopalganj District, Bangladesh, freeing detainees and looting firearms as police fire tear gas and rubber bullets, before the attackers also burn the residence of Bangladesh Nationalist Party Member of Parliament S M Jilani of Gopalganj-3 and blockade local roads. (The Daily Star) (The Business Standard)

2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests Bangladeshi police and 42 platoons of the Border Guard Bangladesh deploy tear gas, stun grenades, batons, and surveillance drones during clashes with thousands of garment workers across Dhaka, Savar, Ashulia, Gazipur, and Narayanganj demanding a monthly minimum wage increase from ৳12,500 (US$100) to ৳30,000 ($240). Protesters block the N3, N4, and N5 highways and force the closure of at least 37 factories after a Minimum Wage Board meeting is postponed to November 23. (AFP) (The Hindu)

Canada–China relations Canada and China agree to further tariff reductions following talks between Canadian prime minister Mark Carney and Chinese leader Xi Jinping before the APEC summit in Shenzhen. China reduces tariffs on C$400 million (¥1.8 billion) in Canadian exports, while Canada extends relief for Chinese steel and aluminium. (AFP)
2026 Russian Air Force Antonov An-12 crash A Russian Air Force Antonov An-12 crash near Kemerovo, Russia, killing all 19 people on board. (The Independent)
Forty-six people are injured after a collision between two trains in Prague, Czech Republic. (BBC News)

Measles resurgence in the Americas The Pan American Health Organization revokes measles elimination status of Bolivia, Mexico, and the United States. For the U.S., the organization cited continuous domestic transmission for over 12 months amid more than 5,700 reported infections and multiple deaths in 2026. (AFP via France 24)

France–Malaysia relations France and Malaysia establish a strategic partnership, signing agreements on defence, energy, and technology cooperation during French president Emmanuel Macron's state visit. Malaysia also agrees to permit limited exports of unprocessed rare-earth minerals to France in exchange for assistance with mineral processing. (Reuters)

Israel–United Kingdom relations UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announces that the UK will sanction eight companies involved in the construction of settlements in the occupied West Bank, as well as Tzav 9 for its role in blocking humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip. (AP)

Corruption in Mongolia Mongolian president Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh announces his resignation from office, three days after former Ulaanbaatar mayor Khishgeegiin Nyambaatar accused him of past embezzlement from a railway project during his tenure as prime minister. The State Great Khural must accept the resignation for it to become effective. (AP)

American technology company Apple experiences an outage with several of its issues, including Apple Pay, iCloud, the App Store, and AppleCare. The company's spokesperson attributed the problems to an internal update and rules out a cyberattack. (Time)
